commitResults.messageTitle: Run JavaFX tests headless only on CI
commitResults.messageBody:
The test task always runs JavaFX through the Monocle headless
platform.

JDKs that bundle JavaFX (e.g. Zulu "fx") cannot load Monocle from the
classpath, so the JavaFX UI tests fail locally even though they pass
on CI.

Let's set the Monocle system properties only when the CI environment
variable is present, and use the normal toolkit for local runs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move student parser tokenizer to shared class
commitResults.messageBody:
StudentAddParser tokenizes its prefixed arguments itself, rejecting
unknown and repeated prefixes.

The upcoming homework commands need the same strict tokenizing, plus
access to the text before the first prefix (e.g. a student index).

Let's move the tokenizing into a reusable StrictArgumentTokenizer that
can either reject or return that preamble, and let StudentAddParser
use it. Add Student behaves exactly as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add strict parsing for displayed indexes
commitResults.messageBody:
ParserUtil#parseIndex accepts signs and leading zeroes, such as "+1"
and "01", and reports a fixed error message.

The homework commands take student and homework indices that must be
plain positive whole numbers, and each index needs its own error
message so users know which one is wrong.

Let's add ParserUtil#parseStrictIndex, which accepts only
[1-9][0-9]* within the int range and throws the given message
otherwise.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow parsing a single tuition subject
commitResults.messageBody:
TuitionSubject can only be parsed as part of a comma-separated
TuitionSubjects list.

Homework belongs to exactly one subject, so the homework commands need
to parse a single subject and report a clear error for an unknown one.

Let's add TuitionSubject#parse, which ignores case and surrounding
whitespace, along with a MESSAGE_CONSTRAINTS listing the valid
subjects.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add homework title and due date fields
commitResults.messageBody:
There is no way to represent the title or the due date of a homework
record.

Tutors need a readable title and a due date for each piece of homework
they assign, and typing the year every time is tedious.

Let's add two value classes:

* Title: 1 to 100 characters with whitespace collapsed, rejecting line
  breaks and control characters, and comparable ignoring case.
* DueDate: a real calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD or MM-DD form, where the
  month and day may have 1 or 2 digits. The year of an MM-DD date is
  inferred as the next occurrence on or after the given day.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add homework record with status and score
commitResults.messageBody:
There is no model class for a homework record.

Tutors assign homework per subject and need to track whether it is
done and, later, what the student scored.

Let's add a Homework class holding a title, subject, due date, status
and optional score, with HomeworkStatus (ASSIGNED, COMPLETED) and a
placeholder Score. Two records are the same homework if their titles
match ignoring case and their subjects and due dates are equal, so
status and score changes do not create a new record.

Add HomeworkBuilder and TypicalHomeworks for tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store homework in each student
commitResults.messageBody:
Student holds only the six profile fields, and the student roster
cannot replace a student once added.

Homework commands need each student to own an ordered list of
homework, and need to swap in an updated copy of the student, since
Student is immutable.

Let's give Student an immutable homework list with helpers to count
assigned homework, detect duplicates and copy the student with a new
list. Add setStudent to StudentRoster, Model and ModelManager to
replace a student in place, rejecting a missing target or a duplicate
identity.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add homework add command
commitResults.messageBody:
Tutors have no way to record homework assigned to a student.

Recording homework against the student who must do it is the first
step towards tracking outstanding work before each lesson.

Let's add `homework add STUDENT_INDEX title/TITLE s/SUBJECT due/DATE`,
with `hw` and `t/` as shorter aliases. The `homework` command word is
handled by a HomeworkCommandParser that dispatches on the subcommand,
so later homework subcommands can plug in. The command rejects a
subject the student does not take and a duplicate homework record.
When the due date omits the year, the inferred year is reported in the
result, and AddressBookParser takes a Clock so tests can fix "today".

Unexpected errors while adding are logged and reported as an internal
error, leaving the roster unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add homework list command
commitResults.messageBody:
Homework can be added to a student, but there is no way to see a
student's homework afterwards.

Tutors need to review what a student has been assigned, and need the
homework indices that later commands such as delete refer to.

Let's add `homework list STUDENT_INDEX` (alias `hw ls`), which shows
the student's homework in insertion order, one numbered line per
record with its title, subject and due date. A student without
homework gets a short message instead of an empty list.

Unexpected errors while listing are logged and reported as an internal
error.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add homework delete command
commitResults.messageBody:
Homework can be added and listed, but a record added by mistake or no
longer relevant cannot be removed.

Let's add `homework delete STUDENT_INDEX HOMEWORK_INDEX` (alias
`hw del`), where HOMEWORK_INDEX is the number shown by `homework
list`. The remaining homework keeps its order. Each index has its own
syntax and range error, so users can tell which index is wrong.

Unexpected errors while deleting are logged and reported as an
internal error, leaving the roster unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add placeholders for homework edit commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The homework feature will also need commands to edit a record, mark
it as completed and record its score, but none of them exist yet.

Let's add placeholder command and parser classes for these three
commands that report "not implemented", so teammates can fill them in
independently. They are not wired into HomeworkCommandParser yet, so
users cannot reach them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Skip address book save for homework commands
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager saves the address book after every command except Add
Student.

Students and their homework are kept in memory only, so the homework
commands change nothing that is saved. Saving after them is wasted
work, and a failing save would wrongly report an error for a command
that succeeded.

Let's skip the save after the homework add, list and delete commands,
as is done for Add Student.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show assigned homework count on student card
commitResults.messageBody:
The student card shows only the six profile fields, so the roster
gives no hint of outstanding homework.

Tutors want to see at a glance which students still have homework to
do, without listing each student's homework.

Let's add an "Assigned homework: N" row to the student card, counting
only homework that is not yet completed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap student card rows to fit the list width
commitResults.messageBody:
Each student card is as wide as its longest row. A long student or
guardian name pushes the badges and contact details past the list's
right edge and adds a horizontal scroll bar.

Let's make the card take its width from the list cell instead: the
name wraps, the index and badges keep their full width, and the
contact details flow onto extra lines when they do not fit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fit main window to 1280x720 at 150% scaling
commitResults.messageBody:
The main window has a minimum height of 600 and a fixed 100-pixel
result box. On a 1280x720 screen at 150% scaling, the window does not
fit, and long results are cut off because the result box neither
wraps nor grows.

Let's lower the minimum window height to 450, let the result box grow
to 180 pixels and wrap its text, and give the roster tabs a minimum
height so the student list stays usable.

commitResults.messageTitle: Select Students tab by default
commitResults.messageBody:
The tab shown at startup is left to TabPane's default selection
rather than chosen by MainWindow.

The student roster is the main page of TutorFlow, and the status bar
text set at startup describes it, so users should always land on it.

Let's select the Students tab explicitly when the window fills its
parts.

commitResults.messageTitle: Close help window with Escape
commitResults.messageBody:
The help window can only be closed with the mouse, and keyboard focus
does not return to the command box afterwards.

TutorFlow is keyboard-first, so users should be able to dismiss help
and keep typing commands without reaching for the mouse.

Let's close the help window when Escape is pressed, and move focus
back to the command box whenever the help window is hidden.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load sample students at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
TutorFlow starts with an empty student roster on every launch, since
students are not saved yet.

New users and testers have to add students and homework by hand
before they can try any student or homework command.

Let's add sample students, most with some homework, and load them into
the roster at every startup. Once students are saved, the samples
should only be used when no data file exists, as for sample persons.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document homework commands in UG and DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide and Developer Guide do not mention homework.

Users need to know the syntax and rules of the new commands, and
developers need to know how homework commands are parsed and where
homework is stored before extending the feature.

Let's document `homework add`, `homework list` and `homework delete`
in the User Guide, with the `|` alternatives notation and command
summary rows. Add a homework management section to the Developer
Guide covering parsing and error order, the model, due date forms and
year inference, error handling, persistence, and the choice of
storing homework inside each Student.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge upstream master into homework branch
commitResults.messageBody:
Upstream lets Add Student keep slashes in student and guardian names
(including the standalone s/o token) and builds a jar that runs on
Windows, macOS and Linux.

Conflicts and how they are resolved:

- build.gradle: keep running JavaFX headless via Monocle only on CI,
  and add upstream's test classpath filter after it so tests still
  load the JavaFX natives for the current platform.
- StudentAddParser: keep using the shared StrictArgumentTokenizer
  instead of upstream's inline loop. The tokenizer gains an optional
  value filter, and Add Student passes upstream's isPartOfName rule
  to it, so names keep their slashes while homework parsing is
  unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test value filter in shared tokenizer
commitResults.messageBody:
The shared tokenizer accepts a value filter that keeps chosen
prefix-shaped tokens inside the preceding value. Add Student relies on
it to keep slashes in names, but the tokenizer's own tests do not
cover the filter.

Let's add tests that check:

- tokens the filter accepts stay in the value, even allowed prefixes
- the filter sees the right previous prefix (null before the first)
- the form without a filter still splits at every prefix
- unknown, repeated and leading-text checks still apply to tokens the
  filter rejects

commitResults.messageTitle: Truncate long contact details on student card
commitResults.messageBody:
A student card is at least as wide as its longest contact detail: the
details sit in a FlowPane, whose minimum width is the full one-line
width of its widest label. A 70-character guardian name thus pushes
the card past the list's right edge whenever that label is wider than
the list. That depends on the font and the window width, so the
card-width test passes on macOS but fails on the Ubuntu CI runner,
whose default font is wider.

Let's give the details pane a zero minimum width and cap each detail
at the pane's width, so a detail too long for the card is shortened
with an ellipsis instead of widening the card.

Let's also make the test independent of the platform's font: size the
list to three quarters of the guardian detail's one-line width, so the
detail never fits on one line, and report the measured edges when an
assertion fails.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show command list inside help window
commitResults.messageBody:
The help window shows only a link to the user guide and a Copy URL
button.

Users must leave the app and open a browser to look up a command
format, which breaks the keyboard-first flow, and the linked guide is
the original AB3 one, not ours.

Let's list the commands inside the help window instead: adding a
student, adding, listing and deleting homework, help and exit, each
with its format, what it does and an example. The window can be
scrolled with the arrow and Page Up/Down keys, and Esc closes it and
returns focus to the command box.

Each format is the command's own usage text, so the help window cannot
drift from the parser error messages, and a test checks that every
example parses. Plain labels in a scroll pane are used rather than a
WebView, which would add a large library to the JAR.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove old contact commands and tab
commitResults.messageBody:
The app still carries the AB3 contact features next to the student
roster. The edit, delete, find and list commands work only on contacts,
and the main window shows the contacts in an Address Book tab.

TutorFlow manages students, and contacts can no longer be added, so
these commands and the tab only confuse tutors.

Let's remove the contact commands with their parsers and tests, and the
Address Book tab with its contact list panel and cards. The student list
now fills the main window on its own.

The contact model and its storage stay for now, as the data file still
holds contacts. A later commit replaces them with students.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move student roster into the address book
commitResults.messageBody:
The model keeps the student roster in a field of its own, next to the
address book. Only the address book is copied, compared and handed to
storage, so the students and their homework sit outside the data that
the app saves.

Saving students needs them to be part of that data first.

Let's hold the student roster in the address book, beside the contacts,
and let the model reach the students through it. The address book can
now replace its whole roster at once, keeping the roster order.

As the clear command empties the whole address book, it now removes all
students too. The next commit makes this behavior official.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clear all students with the clear command
commitResults.messageBody:
The clear command empties the address book, which now holds every
student and their homework. Its message still says the address book was
cleared, and the help window leaves the command out because it used to
reset only the old contacts.

Tutors need to know that clear deletes all their students, and to find
the command in the help window.

Let's say in the success message that all students and their homework
were cleared, and list clear in the help window with a warning that it
cannot be undone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse saved due dates and homework statuses
commitResults.messageBody:
A due date can be read only through the command format, which also
accepts a short MM-DD date and infers its year from today's date. A
homework status has no text form to read back.

Saving homework needs to read both back from the data file, where the
year of a date must not change with the day the app starts.

Let's add a way to read a due date that accepts only the full
YYYY-MM-DD form, and a way to read a status from its name, ignoring
case and surrounding spaces. Both reject invalid text with a message
that says what is allowed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save students and homework instead of contacts
commitResults.messageBody:
The data file holds only the old AB3 contacts, which the app no longer
shows or edits. Students and their homework live in memory only, so
every launch starts again with the sample students, and the student
list warns that nothing is saved.

Tutors lose all their students and homework when they close the app.

Let's save the students in the data file in place of the contacts, and
remove the contact model with its storage, test helpers and test data:

* Save each student with their homework as readable JSON in
  data/tutorflow.json, with full due dates and statuses by name.
* Treat a data file with no students field, an empty or invalid entry,
  or duplicate students as invalid, and start with no students, as
  for any other file that cannot be read.
* Start with the sample students only when there is no data file.
* Save after each command that changes the data, but not after one
  that only reads it, such as homework list.
* Show the data file path in the status bar again, drop the notes that
  students are not saved, and name TutorFlow in the exit message.

The contacts go in the same commit because the model and the data file
switch from contacts to students together.

commitResults.messageTitle: Undo changes when saving fails
commitResults.messageBody:
When a command changes the data but the data file cannot be written,
the command reports the file error, yet its change stays in the app.
The app then shows students or homework that are not in the data file
and that disappear at the next launch.

Tutors should be able to trust that what they see is saved.

Let's take a copy of the data before each command and put it back if
saving fails, so the app again matches the data file. Commands can now
give their own message for a failed save: homework add and delete say
that no homework data was changed. Other commands keep the file error
message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Write the data file atomically
commitResults.messageBody:
Saving writes the new data straight over the data file. If the app
stops or the disk fills up part way, the file is left half written and
cannot be read at the next launch, so the tutor starts with no
students.

Now that the data file holds all students and their homework, a failed
save must never damage the data saved before.

Let's write the data to a temporary file next to the data file first,
and then move it over the data file in one step where the file system
allows. If writing fails, the temporary file is removed and the data
file keeps its old content. Errors name the data file, not the
temporary one.

A read-only data file stays read-only and is reported as such, and an
existing file keeps its permissions. The parent folders are created
when missing, so the separate step that created an empty file first is
no longer needed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject non-integer scores in the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
A homework score in the data file is read as a whole number, so a
score edited by hand to 85.5 is cut down to 85 without any warning,
and a score written as text, such as "85", is read as a number.

A tutor who edits the data file should not have a score changed
silently.

Let's accept only a JSON whole number within the int range as a score,
and treat any other value, such as 85.5, 85.0, "85" or true, as
invalid data with a message saying the score must be a whole number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove parser and text helpers no longer used
commitResults.messageBody:
With the contact commands and model gone, some AB3 helpers have no
callers left outside their own tests: the prefix tokenizer with its
argument map and prefix class, the lenient index parser, the message
for repeated prefixes, the word search and number check on strings,
and the argument check in the app utilities.

Unused code still has to be read, tested and kept in line with the
coding standard.

Let's remove these helpers and their tests. The student and homework
parsers keep using the strict tokenizer and the strict index parser.
The typical test indexes are renamed from persons to students.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update guides and diagrams for saved students
commitResults.messageBody:
The user and developer guides still describe the AB3 contact commands,
the addressbook.json file and a model and storage that hold persons.
They also warn that students and homework are not saved, and several
diagrams show contact classes or the delete command.

The guides are part of the product and must match what the app does.

Let's update the guides and diagrams to match the saved student data:

* User guide: describe TutorFlow, the student add and clear commands,
  automatic saving, the tutorflow.json format and its rules, and drop
  the contact commands and the not-saved warning.
* Developer guide: describe the student model, the JSON storage and
  its load rules, saving after a command with the undo on failure, and
  atomic writes, with design considerations.
* Redraw the UI, Logic, parser, Model, Storage and architecture
  diagrams, and replace the delete sequence diagram with one for
  homework delete.
* Replace the UI mockup on the home page with a screenshot of the
  current main window.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fit main window parts at minimum window size
commitResults.messageBody:
The main window's minimum size is 600x450, but its parts need more
height than the scene such a window leaves. On native Windows, the
scene is 587x414.5 while the status bar ends at y=426, so the warning
that student changes are not saved is cut off.

Let's lower the roster tabs' minimum height from 230 to 200 pixels,
leaving about 18 pixels to spare on Windows. The window keeps its
450-pixel minimum height so that it still fits a 1280x720 screen at
150% scaling.

Add a test that checks the window's parts fit in that Windows scene.
As this is the second test class that starts JavaFX, both classes now
tolerate JavaFX having been started already in the same test JVM.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use sample students in homework add examples
commitResults.messageBody:
Three of the User Guide's homework add examples fail on a fresh launch
with "The selected student does not take this subject.": student 2
takes MATH and CHEMISTRY, and student 3 takes only MATH, so they cannot
get PHYSICS or CHEMISTRY homework.

Let's give the PHYSICS examples to student 1, who takes PHYSICS, and
the CHEMISTRY example to student 2.

Add a test that runs every homework example in the guide on the
sample students that TutorFlow starts with, so the examples and the
sample data stay in step.

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete partial parameter docs in homework code
commitResults.messageBody:
Some Javadoc comments added for homework management tag only some
parameters. The Homework constructor, for example, tags only score,
while the SE-EDU Java standard asks for all parameters or none.

Let's tag every parameter where at least one needs explaining: the
nullable score of Homework, the two different index lists of
HomeworkDeleteCommand, and the preamble switch and token filter of
the private StrictArgumentTokenizer#tokenize.

Methods whose names and summary already explain each parameter keep
no parameter tags.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update user guide add examples for students
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide documents `add` as AB3's person command, with name,
phone, email, address and tag fields. Since the add student feature,
`add` takes a student's name, academic level, subjects, phone, and
guardian's name and phone, so every `add` example in the guide fails
with "Invalid command format."

Let's document the student `add` command in the quick start, the
renamed "Adding a student" section and the command summary: its six
required prefixes, the rules for each field and duplicate students,
and examples that use several subjects, any field order and a
guardian name with `s/o`.

Show command list inside help window

The help window shows only a link to the user guide and a Copy URL
button. Users have to leave the app to look up a command format, which
breaks the keyboard-first flow, and the link points to the original
AB3 guide.

Let's list every command in the help window instead, grouped into
Students, Homework and General, each with its format, a short
description and an example. The window scrolls with the keyboard as
soon as it opens, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the
command box.

The formats come from each command's MESSAGE_USAGE, so the help window
cannot drift from the parsers' error messages. Plain labels in a
scroll pane are used rather than a WebView, to keep the JAR small.

Closes #40

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'master' into enable-persistence-for-new-schemas
Start with no students if the data file holds null
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file that holds only the JSON value null is read by Jackson as
a null object. JsonUtil#readJsonFile then throws NullPointerException,
which escapes the startup recovery for invalid data files, so
TutorFlow does not start.

Let's treat a null file like any other invalid JSON file, so that
TutorFlow starts with no students, as the User Guide says it does for
an invalid data file. The preferences file is read the same way, so it
falls back to the default preferences instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save through a temporary file with a unique name
commitResults.messageBody:
To save the data file, FileUtil#writeToFile writes to the fixed
sibling path tutorflow.json.tmp and moves it over the data file. A
file the user keeps under that name is overwritten and moved away,
and an empty folder under that name is deleted when the save fails.

A save should change no file other than the data file.

Let's create the temporary file with Files#createTempFile, which picks
a name no other file has, and clean up only that file after a
failure. Such a file can be read and written only by its owner on
POSIX file systems, so a new data file now gets those permissions,
which suits the students' and guardians' contact details it holds.
An existing data file keeps its permissions as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the data file's Windows access list on save
commitResults.messageBody:
Saving replaces the data file with a new temporary file. On POSIX file
systems, the temporary file gets the data file's permissions first,
but on Windows it gets the folder's inherited access control list. A
data file that only its owner may read becomes readable by everyone
the folder allows after the next save.

The file holds students' and guardians' contact details, so a save
must not change who can read it.

Let's copy the data file's access control list to the temporary file
as well, wherever the file system supports one, and copy permissions
before the data is written rather than after. The new test runs only
on file systems with access control lists, i.e. on Windows.

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete partial parameter docs in storage code
commitResults.messageBody:
The JSON constructors of JsonAdaptedHomework and JsonAdaptedStudent
document only one of their parameters, and so does
JsonAddressBookStorage#saveAddressBook(ReadOnlyAddressBook, Path).

The coding standard asks for @param tags for all parameters or none.

Let's document all of them, as the score, the homework list and the
file path each need an explanation that the method summary cannot
give, and every JSON field may be null when it is missing from the
file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Docs: Sync homework and lesson details with code
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG and DG describe homework and lessons in ways that no longer
match the app. The DG says lessons are not implemented, the UG omits
the real homework list output, and the manual tests do not cover
saving lessons.

Readers rely on the guides to use and extend the app, so wrong or
missing details mislead both users and developers.

Let's bring both guides in line with the code:

UG:
* Show the real homework list output, its empty case, and that the
  list includes completed homework without showing the status
* Note that the student card count excludes completed homework
* Explain how the year is inferred for 29 February
* State that delete also removes the student's regular lessons
* Warn that misspelled optional data-file keys are silently ignored

DG:
* Drop "lessons are not implemented" from the Model component
* Mention lessons in the Storage component and the JSON lessons keys
* State that lesson listing is implemented by LessonListCommand
* Add LessonAddCommand to the commands overriding the save-failure
  message
* Extend the saving manual test to cover lessons

All new examples and messages were run in the app and copied from its
output.

commitResults.messageBody: Refactor legacy AB3 code and remove unused components

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove homework status
commitResults.messageBody:
Each homework record has a status, ASSIGNED or COMPLETED, but no
command can change it, and the student card counts only the records
that are still assigned. The planned status command has been dropped.

A status that can never be set misleads the user: every new homework
stays ASSIGNED forever, so the card count only ever grows.

Let's remove the status from the model, the data file, the sample
data and the docs, together with the unused status command
placeholders. The student card now shows "Upcoming homework: N", the
number of records due today or later, which stays meaningful without
a status.

Data files that still contain a "status" key load as before; the key
is ignored and dropped on the next save.

Part of #41

commitResults.messageTitle: Record homework score as marks out of a total
commitResults.messageBody:
A homework score is a single whole number, so TutorFlow cannot tell
whether 8 means 8 out of 10 or 8 out of 100.

Tutors mark homework out of different totals, and the planned marks
command records the marks obtained together with the total.

Let's store the score as MARKS_OBTAINED/TOTAL_MARKS, e.g. 5/10, and
keep the ratio as given rather than simplify it. A score needs a
positive total and marks obtained from zero to the total, with whole
numbers no greater than 2147483647. The data file keeps the score as
the text "5/10" so it stays easy to edit by hand.

A file with an old single-number score such as 85 is rejected, like
any other invalid file.

Part of #41

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to edit a student's homework
commitResults.messageBody:
A homework record cannot be changed once added. A tutor who mistypes
a title or moves a deadline must delete the record and add it again,
which also loses its score and moves it to the end of the list.

Let's add `homework edit` (alias `hw e`), which changes the title,
subject or due date of one record while keeping its position and its
score. It follows the rules of `homework add`: the same prefixes,
date forms and year inference, error messages and check order, and

no total, so it loads as no score and a warning is logged.

score loses data the tutor entered.

ratio. The bare number follows the rules of each number in a ratio and
is shown as entered, so 17 and 17/20 are different scores. The invalid

the score 85, which is saved back as text. A JSON number that is not a
valid score, such as 85.5, -3 or 3000000000, is still dropped with a
warning, so the rest of the file loads. A JSON number is checked by the
same rules as its digits written as text, so both forms accept the same
scores.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let quoted values contain prefix-like words
commitResults.messageBody:
Every prefixed value is cut at the next lowercase word followed by a
slash, so a homework title such as "Speed in km/h" or a name that
contains an allowed prefix is rejected as an unknown or repeated
prefix. The only workaround is to change the text, e.g. "km / h".

Let's let users wrap a value in double quotes. The shared tokenizer
skips prefix-like words inside a quoted value and removes the outer
quotes before the value is validated, so student add, lesson and
homework commands all accept it. A quoted value ends at the first
quote followed by the end of the input, or by whitespace and one of
the command's own prefixes; other quotes are kept as typed. A value
without such a closing quote is read as before, and unquoted input
parses exactly as before.

Ending at the first quote that is followed by a real prefix lets a
title hold both quotes and a word like km/, which ending at the next
quote cannot; escape characters were left out to keep typing simple.

commitResults.messageTitle: Strip spaces inside quoted values
commitResults.messageBody:

value without quotes is stripped. So `hw up due/" 3 "` is rejected,
although `hw up due/ 3 ` is accepted, and a stray space typed inside
the quotes can make a value invalid.

Quotes are there to keep prefix-like words in a value, not to change
how the rest of the value is read.

Let's strip the text inside the quotes as well, keeping the spaces
between words: `n/" Ravi s/o Kumar "` gives `Ravi s/o Kumar`. Empty
quotes, or quotes with only spaces inside, give an empty value, which
each command treats like a prefix with nothing after it. The user
guide's notes about the command format and the developer guide's

the new rule.

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve typed FXML loading failures
commitResults.messageBody:
FXML loading wraps I/O failures in AssertionError, which prevents the
student view from recovering without also catching programming errors.

Propagate those failures as UncheckedIOException with their original
cause. This gives the rendering boundary a recoverable exception while
leaving genuine assertion failures visible.

Update loader expectations and validate all UI tests and Checkstyle.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle recoverable student card rendering failures
commitResults.messageBody:
JavaFX can render student cells after command execution, outside the
command's exception handler.

Handle recoverable cell failures at the student panel boundary. Clear
the failed graphic, log the technical cause once per rendering attempt
and notify the owner without changing student records.

Keep assertion failures visible. Add an injectable card factory and
focused JavaFX tests for recovery and diagnostic logging.

Validate the panel and existing student UI tests with Checkstyle.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report filter rendering failures in the UI
commitResults.messageBody:
Rendering can fail during a roster update or later when JavaFX creates
a cell. Command success feedback must not hide either failure.

Connect the panel's recovery callback to the result display and retain
its error message when rendering fails during command execution.
Allow a later command to begin a fresh rendering attempt.

Add UI tests for consecutive indices, result counts, invalid-command
selection and viewport preservation, deferred failures and recovery.
Realize selection styling before recording the viewport position.

Validate all UI regression tests and Checkstyle.

commitResults.messageBody:

commitResults.messageTitle: Add stable student sorting rules
commitResults.messageBody:

meeting day without changing student records or dropping occurrences.

Cover school levels, multiple values, ties and duplicate occurrences.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate displayed student order from roster order
commitResults.messageBody:
A filtered view follows stored order and cannot retain an independent
student sort. Reordering the stored roster would also trigger a save.

Reset its order whenever a filter establishes a new result set so list
and search retain their existing ordering contracts.

Related to #78

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve student view state during sort rendering
commitResults.messageBody:

alone cannot verify that sorting preserves the UI after a render error.

checking all candidate cards and visible cell layout. Record callback
failures for recovery and refresh card indices when cells move.

Related to #78

commitResults.messageTitle: Recover student sorts at the UI boundary
commitResults.messageBody:
A completed model sort can still fail while JavaFX renders its cards.
Reporting success before checking that rendering leaves the displayed
order and selection inconsistent with the reported command outcome.

Verify sort rendering before reporting success. Restore the prior order
and view on failure, preserve retry input and log the technical cause
once at WARNING after recovery or SEVERE if restoration also fails.

Related to #78

commitResults.messageBody:

student or that a display-only command avoids persistence calls.

one technical failure record without leaving altered logger settings.

Related to #78

commitResults.messageTitle: Document student sorting and recovery diagnostics

commitResults.messageTitle: Harden sort recovery and week-boundary tests
commitResults.messageBody:
A renderer or model can throw the same exception instance again during
recovery. Self-suppression must not hide that failed restoration or
incorrectly classify it as a recovered warning.

Retain explicit recovery-failure context for that case. Add regression
checks for week boundaries, equal-day times and zero persistence calls
after an internal sorting failure.

Related to #78

and keep sort rollback responsible for its own diagnostics. Remove the

Related to #78

commitResults.messageTitle: Unify filter and sort rendering diagnostics
commitResults.messageBody:
A filter following a sort can publish predicate and order changes in
one command. Resetting diagnostics on each update logs the same render
failure twice and splits a single recovery attempt.

Keep one rendering attempt for the full command and release it in a
finally block. Preserve independent updates and deferred error reports.
Add regressions for filtered sorting, order resets, displayed indices,
empty results, rollback and diagnostic ownership.

Related to #78

predicate still matches, and that another explicit sort uses the new
values. Add regression tests for level, subject and meeting-day changes
and for a replacement leaving the active filter.

Keep this behavior consistent with existing lesson and homework updates
so an edit does not unexpectedly move a displayed student.

commitResults.messageBody:

actual widths. On Linux, a wrapped section heading needs more height
and can leave the homework list clipped.

widths so divider movement keeps both lists in bounds. Document the
sizing rule and allow one pixel for layout rounding in the regression.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reserve sidebar height at its minimum width
commitResults.messageBody:

Basing the minimum on its displayed width leaves the outer split pane
with a smaller minimum after the horizontal divider moves on Linux.

Reserve the height required at each section's narrowest permitted width
so both lists fit throughout divider movement. Keep the computed bound
in assertion diagnostics and document the sizing rule.

Validation: full check and coverage pass on Windows and headless Linux.
The 17-command rendered JavaFX smoke test passes again on Windows.
